part.text:
Done. I implemented the solution in both files:

**`kindergarten_garden.h`** — declares the `Plants` enum (`clover`, `grass`, `violets`, `radishes`) and `plants(const std::string& diagram, const std::string& student)` returning `std::array<Plants, 4>`.

**`kindergarten_garden.cpp`** — the implementation:
- Splits the diagram string on `'\n'` into the two rows (first row = nearest the windows).
- Looks the student up in the fixed alphabetical list (Alice … Larry) to get their index.
- Each child's cups are at columns `index * 2` and `index * 2 + 1` in each row, returned in order: first row pair, then second row pair.
- Maps `G`/`C`/`R`/`V` to the corresponding `Plants` value.

I tried to build and run the test suite, but shell execution was denied in this session, so I couldn't execute the tests myself. The logic matches the spec examples (e.g. `"RC\nGG"` for Alice → radishes, clover, grass, grass; the 24-cup diagram for Bob → clover, grass, clover, clover). If you can allow shell access, I can run `cmake -S . -B build -DEXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS=ON`, build, and run the binary to confirm all tests pass.
